assertion.rationale: F9 (Task 13): platform/main.bicep routes diagnosticSettings for Key Vault (AuditEvent -- the estate's only real credentials), the cost-export storage account (account-level metrics and blob-service-level data-plane logs), the SQL database (Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases, not the server resource -- verified against the avm/res/sql/server@0.22.0 module schema, which has no top-level diagnosticSettings param) and the Container Apps environment, all to the Log Analytics workspace. SQL auditSettings sets isAzureMonitorTargetEnabled: true, so the previously-nominal audit (state: Enabled, no destination) actually writes somewhere. layer-06-platform.yml routes the subscription Activity Log (Administrative/Security/Policy/etc.) and Entra ID SignInLogs/AuditLogs to the same workspace. Both were relocated from the brief's named files (layer-02-landing-zone.yml, layer-03-entra.yml) to layer-06-platform.yml: on a full infra-up.yml pass, L2 and L3 both precede L6, so the Log Analytics workspace either setting must reference does not exist yet at those points -- a same-pass invariant (infra-up.yml also supports a skip-tolerant selective replay, so this is not claimed as universal), not a reason to leave either unwired. A first pass deferred the Entra item as unverifiable without a live tenant; review corrected that -- the Microsoft.aadiam tenant-scoped resource shape and the required Security Administrator Entra role are both publicly documented (Microsoft Learn), so it is implemented with the same az monitor diagnostic-settings create verb the Activity Log step uses. One recorded, separate loose end, following the F20/F21 precedent (a grant expressed in code without a live check that its precondition holds): nothing in this repo's IaC currently grants mls-github-deployer the Security Administrator role that step needs at runtime, so whether it succeeds in a live tenant is unverified -- noted in the step's own comment, not a reason this control stays open, the same way F20 (SQL grant expressed, application unverified) did not keep F13 open for the grants that had no such caveat. A prior pass also downgraded this control's gapSeverity from high to medium on the reasoning that most of F9's items had landed; that was reverted on review, citing 3.1.5.json's own precedent (F13 five-of-seven landed, severity held at high) -- severity does not discount for partial progress. With Entra now also implemented, F9 has no remaining open contributor, so this control closes outright rather than landing on a discounted GAP. Checked: no other finding in compliance/findings/2026-08-26-prepublication-review.md cites 3.3.1.

recommendation: None outstanding for this control. A regression here -- diagnosticSettings removed from any of Key Vault/storage/SQL/CAE, SQL auditSettings losing isAzureMonitorTargetEnabled, or either subscription-scope/tenant-scope diagnostic setting dropped from layer-06-platform.yml -- would reopen it. The unverified Security Administrator prerequisite for the Entra step (see that step's comment in layer-06-platform.yml) is worth a live-tenant check but is not itself a reason to reopen this control, consistent with how F20/F21 were handled under F13.
